**Finding: Deviation (critical) — INDEMN**

Section 12 runs heavily one way. Section 12.a imposes a broad indemnity on us (Client) covering breach, System/Credit Repository defaults caused by us or our customers, all Web Site/Client Content claims "without regard to any knowledge limitation," and product/service injury claims. By contrast, TrueLink's indemnity in §12.b is confined to its own breach of the Agreement or failure to perform — it contains **no third-party IP infringement indemnity**, no breach-of-law indemnity, no data-compromise indemnity, and nothing for gross negligence or willful misconduct. The only non-infringement covenants in the document (§2 domain names, §8 Client Content) run *from* us, so nothing elsewhere fills the gap.

**Redline (validated, preferred level):** expanded §12.b so TrueLink also indemnifies us for (ii) allegations that the Interface, Hosting Services, Support Services or other TrueLink-supplied software/materials infringe or misappropriate IP; (iii) TrueLink's breach of applicable law; (iv) unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content, Credit Data or other Client data caused by TrueLink; and (v) TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct — plus a standard mutual notice/control/cooperation procedure with a no-adverse-settlement consent right.

Note for negotiation: the liability cap in §12 (p0077) applies only to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11, so the indemnity is presently uncapped on both sides. If TrueLink resists the preferred position, the playbook fallback is an IP indemnity with usual exclusions (our modifications, combinations, specifications) and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, optionally subject to a 3× annual fees super-cap.
